The value of this technique is that it provides a preset starting time point for log tools like LogUI, allowing direct extraction of log entries from 5 seconds before and after the crash without manually calculating a time range. vmki7e:263: Among the four common launch crash causes, "Failed to open document" is the hardest type to find evidence for in the logs. This is because the only process that knows what error occurred is the app itself, and third-party apps usually don't write meaningful information to the logs. Unlike code-signing errors (where the whole system performs multi-layer validation) or translocation (where the OS explicitly records the path change), document-open failure depends entirely on the app's own logging awareness. This means that for apps lacking good logging practices, the only diagnostic tool left is cross-validation: indirectly inferring the problem by ruling out the other three more obvious crash causes.
